richSourceAlignedText: Original IM2021 G5 U08:L09 models rain falling on a source EIGHT-SIDED orthogonal roof, unit conversion centimeters to meters and cubic centimeters to liters, and open water-demand and reservoir design questions.

Warm-up Notice and Wonder Cubic Centimeters and Grams uses original credited image. Student explains why a cubic centimeter of water roughly corresponds to one gram under usual conditions; figure credit and measurement assumptions need teacher check.

Activity1 Catching Rainfall includes a roof diagram with printed sides including10m,15m,3m and8m but other sides are UNLABELED/figure-dependent in accessible original text. No exact roof surface area is certified from that partial description alone. With monthly rain depth5cm=0.05m, a hypothetical 1m² patch receives0.05m³=50000cm³=50L of rain. For actual roof, multiply its geometrically verified m² area by50L/m²; account for roof shape and measured dimensions.

Activity1 also asks students to choose RESERVOIR dimensions, which are open and must fit proposed target volume with clear units. Students might make different valid measurements and container designs.

Activity2 How Much Water? original household water-use estimate, required rainfall, engineering challenges and whether rainwater capture is sensible have no single correct answer without the learner's own data. Digital selected choices verify source unit conversion only; teacher evaluates authentic environmental reasoning.
